title: The Transformer Family Version 2.0
excerpt: Lilian Weng updates her canonical transformer survey with sparse attention, long-context variants, state-space hybrids, and the architectural trade-offs that matter for modern LLMs. It remains the best single post for mapping encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder families, though some frontier variants postdate the 2023 write-up.
author: Lilian Weng

title: Optimizing your LLM in production
excerpt: Hugging Face walks through the production bottlenecks of LLM inference—quadratic attention memory, KV-cache growth, positional encoding choices, and Flash Attention—with concrete guidance for deployment. The recommendations reflect the HF/TGI stack circa publication and may omit vendor-specific serving features added later.
author: Hugging Face
coverAlt: LLM optimization diagram from Hugging Face

title: The State of Reasoning
excerpt: Nathan Lambert surveys how reasoning models, RL post-training, and benchmark inflation changed the open-model landscape in late 2024, separating marketing claims from reproducible capability gains. The post is opinionated toward open-weight labs and predates several 2025–2026 reasoning releases.
author: Nathan Lambert

title: Patterns for Building LLM-based Systems & Products
excerpt: Eugene Yan catalogs recurring design patterns for LLM products—routing, caching, guardrails, eval loops, and human-in-the-loop fallbacks—grounded in applied ML systems experience rather than research novelty. The patterns are descriptive, not prescriptive benchmarks, and predate agent-native architectures.
author: Eugene Yan

title: Large language models are having a Stable Diffusion moment
excerpt: Simon Willison explains why locally runnable LLMs felt like Stable Diffusion all over again—sudden capability jumps, messy tooling, and a flood of experiments—and outlines practical ways developers can explore models safely. The 2023 framing remains useful history even as hosted APIs narrowed the gap.
author: Simon Willison

title: LLM Inference at scale with TGI
excerpt: Martín Iglesias dissects Hugging Face Text Generation Inference from warmup through continuous batching, KV caching, and Paged Attention, using Adyen's production deployment as a case study. Throughput numbers are tied to specific hardware and TGI versions from the write-up period.
author: Martín Iglesias
